page: Zod Mini tree-shakable variant of Zod with functional API. Import from zod/mini or @zod/mini standalone package. Same functionality as regular Zod but using functions instead of methods for tree-shaking. Example: z.nullable(z.optional(z.string())) vs z.string().optional().nullable(). Bundle size reduction: 64% smaller for simple boolean parse (2.12kb vs 5.91kb gzipped). Tree-shaking removes unused code; bundlers cannot remove unused methods but can remove unused functions. Use cases: frontend with slow mobile connections. Not recommended for backend or if bundle size < 10kb not significant. Less discoverable DX than regular Zod. Base class ZodMiniType extends core.$ZodType. Questions: What is Zod Mini? How much smaller is bundle? When should I use Zod Mini? What checks are available? What methods does ZodMiniType have?

sections.manifest: Tree-shaking or dead-code elimination. Regular Zod schemas provide convenience methods bundlers cannot remove. Zod Mini uses top-level functions which bundlers can tree-shake. Example regular Zod: z.string().min(5).max(10).trim() becomes z.string().check(z.minLength(5), z.maxLength(10), z.trim()). Bundle sizes: simple boolean parse with Zod Mini 2.12kb gzipped vs Zod 5.91kb (64% reduction). Object schema with Zod Mini 4.0kb vs Zod 13.1kb (69% reduction). Provides understanding of relative bundle sizes.

Use regular Zod unless very strict bundle size constraints. Bundle size on scale of Zod (5-10kb) only meaningful for frontend optimizing for slow mobile in rural/developing areas. Backend development: bundle size not meaningful even on Lambda - 17kb gzipped Zod adds only ~0.6ms cold start. DX: Mini API more verbose, less discoverable, harder to discover methods via Intellisense than chained APIs. Cannot quickly build schemas with chained methods. Internet speed: round trip to server (100-200ms) dwells download time for 10kb. Only on slow 3G (sub-1Mbps) does extra 10kb become significant.

ZodMiniType base class for all Mini schemas, extends z.core.$ZodType. Parse methods: parse, parseAsync, safeParse, safeParseAsync (same as regular Zod). .check() method passes checks as arguments: z.minLength(5), z.maxLength(10), z.refine(), z.trim(). Check functions: z.lt(value), z.lte/z.maximum(value), z.gt(value), z.gte/z.minimum(value), z.positive(), z.negative(), z.nonpositive(), z.nonnegative(), z.multipleOf(value), z.maxSize(value), z.minSize(value), z.size(value), z.maxLength(value), z.minLength(value), z.length(value), z.regex(regex), z.lowercase(), z.uppercase(), z.includes(value), z.startsWith(value), z.endsWith(value), z.property(key, schema), z.mime(value). Custom checks: z.refine(), z.check() (replaces superRefine). Mutations (no type change): z.overwrite(value => newValue), z.normalize(), z.trim(), z.toLowerCase(), z.toUpperCase(). Metadata: z.meta(), z.describe(). Other methods: .register() for registries, .brand() for branded types, .clone(def) for cloning schemas.

No default locale. Regular Zod loads English (en) locale automatically. Zod Mini does not load locale to reduce bundle size when error messages unnecessary, localized to non-English, or customized. Default issue message: 'Invalid input'. Load English locale with z.config(z.locales.en()). Refer to Locales docs for localization.
